subject: Port Jackson shark
title: Cameras Meant for Lobsters Caught Sharks Crushing Sea Urchins

scenes.text: Scientists hid cameras to catch lobsters killing urchins. Something else showed up.
They tied one hundred spiny sea urchins outside a lobster den in Australia.
Lobsters are meant to be the urchin's main enemy. They ate just four percent.
Then sharks came in at night and ate forty-five percent.
Port Jackson and horn sharks went in from the spiny side, some finishing in a few gulps.
Even urchins over twelve centimetres wide. The lobsters mostly walked right past.

description:
Researchers from the University of Newcastle tethered 100 long-spined sea urchins outside a lobster den off Wollongong, New South Wales, for 25 nights, expecting eastern rock lobsters to eat them.
Lobsters ate about 4%, while Port Jackson and crested horn sharks ate about 45%, attacking from the spiny side and handling urchins over 12 cm wide. The study appeared in Frontiers in Marine Science.
Could sharks help save kelp forests from urchins?
first_comment: Some sharks started eating before sunset, before the cameras even switched on. Would you eat something covered in spines?
